sources.entry: Clendar - Clendar is an universal calendar app. Written in SwiftUI.

summary.one_liner: Clendar is a minimal calendar app for Apple platforms, written in SwiftUI, with widgets, keyboard shortcuts, and natural language event parsing.
summary.what_it_does: Clendar is a calendar app for iOS, iPadOS, Catalyst and watchOS, converted from UIKit to SwiftUI by its author. The README lists features including home-screen widgets with dark/light themes, keyboard shortcuts, Siri shortcuts, Apple Watch complications, custom app icons, natural language parsing, a lunar day view, built-in dark and light modes, accessibility support, and localizations. The stack named includes WidgetKit, SiriKit, EventKit (via the author's Shift wrapper), WatchKit, Combine, StoreKit, Fastlane, CocoaPods and Swift Package Manager. The repo is split into app, test, watch extension and a Packages folder holding the theme and SwiftUI calendar view. The README also includes a note from the author that maintenance has paused for personal reasons.
use_cases: Viewing and managing a personal calendar on iPhone or iPad
Adding calendar events with natural language input
Putting calendar widgets on the home screen
Using a calendar on Apple Watch
Studying a SwiftUI calendar app as a learning reference
Reading a lunar calendar day view
how_to_run: Open the Xcode project in Xcode 13.1 or later
On an Apple Silicon Mac, run: sudo arch -x86_64 gem install ffi
Alternatively, run Terminal with Rosetta and run pod install
Install Ruby if you want to use Fastlane build automation
notable: Converted from a UIKit codebase to SwiftUI, and its README documents the move
Widgets with customizable dark and light themes
Natural language parsing for adding events
Uses the author's own Swift packages Shift (EventKit wrapper) and Laden (loading indicator)
caveats: The author says maintenance has been paused for personal reasons, so updates may be slow
Building on Apple Silicon Macs needs an x86_64 workaround with Rosetta and CocoaPods
Requires Xcode 13.1, iOS 15.0 and watchOS 8.0 as minimum versions named in the README
